title: Nifty price-to-book valuation hits pre-Covid level. Why the index is still not cheap
body: The Nifty 50's valuation reset has pushed its price-to-book ratio below 3 times for the first time in nearly six years. title: Infosys, Vedanta among 10 stocks that saw the sharpest decrease in LIC holdings in Q1. See full list
body: Life Insurance Corporation of India has notably trimmed its investments across several leading firms. The reductions in shareholdings were particularly pronounced in Infosys and Vedanta during the latest quarter. Other corporations such as Oil & Natural Gas Corporation and Tata Consultancy Services also reported diminished stakes. Additionally, firms like HCL Technologies and Reliance Industries saw similar decreases. These strategic portfolio adjustments highlight evolving market dynamics and investor approaches.

title: Retail investors make Rs 18,000 crore bold contra bet on 6 falling bluechip stocks. Will it pay off?
body: Retail investors used the June quarter decline in some of India's biggest companies to mount an estimated Rs 17,914 crore contrarian bet, accumulating shares of Infosys , Reliance Industries , TCS , Wipro , HCL Technologies and ITC even as all six stocks fell. #sr_widget.onDemand p, #stock_pro.onDemand p{font-size: 14px;line-height: 1.28;} .onDemand .live_stock{left:17px;padding:1px 3px 1px 5px;font-size:12px;font-weight:600;line-height:18px;top:9px} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc{margin:0 auto 0;} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc{color: #024d99;margin-top:10px;} #sr_widget.onDemand .crypto .live_stock .lb-icon{8px 6px 5px 3px !important} #sr_widget.crypto.onDemand a.text{border-bottom:1px solid #ccc;padding-bottom:5px;display:block;width:100%} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc .text p, #stock_pro.onDemand .sr_desc .text p{font-size:12px;font-weight:400;} The wager is heavily concentrated in technology, the sector most exposed to uncertain global corporate spending and AI disruption. Infosys , TCS , Wipro and HCL Technologies attracted an estimated Rs 12,230 crore, accounting for more than two-thirds of the buying across the six stocks, shows data from PRIME Database.

title: Vodafone Idea shares jump 3% after Q1 net loss narrows. What is Nomura saying?
body: Shares of Vodafone Idea gained 3% to Rs 13.27 on the BSE on Tuesday after the debt-laden telecom operator reported a sharp reduction in its consolidated loss for the first quarter. The company's loss narrowed to Rs 3,754 crore in Q1, compared with Rs 6,608 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue from operations rose 6% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 11,689 crore. #sr_widget.onDemand p, #stock_pro.onDemand p{font-size: 14px;line-height: 1.28;} .onDemand .live_stock{left:17px;padding:1px 3px 1px 5px;font-size:12px;font-weight:600;line-height:18px;top:9px} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc{margin:0 auto 0;} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc{color: #024d99;margin-top:10px;} #sr_widget.onDemand .crypto .live_stock .lb-icon{8px 6px 5px 3px !important} #sr_widget.crypto.onDemand a.text{border-bottom:1px solid #ccc;padding-bottom:5px;display:block;width:100%} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc .text p, #stock_pro.onDemand .sr_desc .text p{font-size:12px;font-weight:400;} EBITDA increased 9% YoY to Rs 5,034 crore from Rs 4,612 crore. The EBITDA margin improved to 43.1% from 41.8% in Q1FY26 and remained unchanged from 43.1% in Q4FY26. Average revenue per user (ARPU) climbed 10.2% to Rs 195 from Rs 177 in the year-ago quarter. Vodafone Idea said this was the highest ARPU growth in the industry.

body: The Indian stock market slipped into the red on Tuesday as rising oil prices amid growing concerns over the Middle East tensions spooked investors. #sr_widget.onDemand p, #stock_pro.onDemand p{font-size: 14px;line-height: 1.28;} .onDemand .live_stock{left:17px;padding:1px 3px 1px 5px;font-size:12px;font-weight:600;line-height:18px;top:9px} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc{margin:0 auto 0;} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc{color: #024d99;margin-top:10px;} #sr_widget.onDemand .crypto .live_stock .lb-icon{8px 6px 5px 3px !important} #sr_widget.crypto.onDemand a.text{border-bottom:1px solid #ccc;padding-bottom:5px;display:block;width:100%} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc .text p, #stock_pro.onDemand .sr_desc .text p{font-size:12px;font-weight:400;} Sensex fell over 300 points to 78,215, while Nifty 50 over 50 points to slip below 24,550, as seen at 9.25 am. Broader markets however remained in the green, with Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 indices rising up to 0.4%.
